mappings.note: Both contain the superscription: 'To the choir director. With flutes. A Psalm of David.' (OSMAIN) vs Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'Hear my words, O Lord; consider my sighing.' (OSMAIN v2) vs Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'Give ear to the sound of my cry... for unto Thee do I pray.' (OSMAIN v3) vs Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'O Lord, in the morning Thou hearest my voice... I will watch for Thee.' (OSMAIN v4) vs Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'For Thou art not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness... evil shall not dwell with Thee.' (OSMAIN v5) vs Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'The boastful shall not stand before Thine eyes... Thou hatest all workers of iniquity.' (OSMAIN v6) vs Hebrew equivalent.
Both contain: 'Thou destroyest them that speak lies... The Lord abhorreth the blood-thirsty and deceitful.' (OSMAIN v7) vs Hebrew equivalent.

Both contain: 'Condemn them... Let them fall by their own counsels; cast them out for the multitude of their transgressions.' (OSMAIN v11) vs Hebrew equivalent.

Translation verse 12 contains the first part of OSMAIN v12 ('Let all that take refuge in Thee rejoice...'), but also includes text found in Translation verse 13. Wait, looking closer: WLC v12 ends with 'and let them who love Thy name exult in Thee.' This matches OSMAIN v12 exactly up to the end of the sentence structure in Norwegian ('fryde seg i deg'). However, standard Hebrew numbering often splits this differently or includes a final blessing. Let's re-examine WLC v13.

This verse contains text NOT present in the provided OSMAIN list (which ends at v12). The content is: 'For Thou blessest the righteous; O Lord, Thou coverest him with favor as with a shield.' This indicates OSMAIN is missing this final blessing or it was merged differently. In many translations, Psalm 5 has 13 verses where the last verse of WLC (v13) corresponds to an additional sentence not in the provided Norwegian text block.

extraContent.description: The mapping for v12 is actually 'exact' if we consider standard verse breaks. However, looking at WLC v13: 'כִּי-אַתָּה תְבָרֵךְ צַדִּיק יְהוָה כַצִנָּה רָצוֹן תַעטְרֶנוּ' (For Thou blessest the righteous; O Lord, with favor as a shield Thou coverest him). This text is completely absent from OSMAIN v1-v12. Therefore, WLC has an extra verse.
Contains unique content: 'For Thou blessest the righteous; O Lord, with favor as a shield Thou coverest him.' This text is missing from the OSMAIN source provided (which stops at v12).
